1. open the starwars dataset in tidyverse
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
data(starwars)
```

2. create a graph showing the frequency of eye colors in the dataset. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color)) + geom_bar()

```

3. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(eye_color)) + geom_bar(fill= "lightblue", color="black") + theme_classic() + xlab("Eye Color") + ylab("Frequency") + ggtitle("Starwars Eye Colors")
```

4. Create a graph displaying information about character's height in each homeworld. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(height, homeworld)) + geom_point()
```

5. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(homeworld, height)) + geom_point(shape=1, color="plum") + theme_bw() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)) + xlab("Homeworld") +  ylab("Height (cm)") + ggtitle("Height by Homeworld")

#I looked up R code for how to change the orientation of variables on the x-axis, because before they were all overlapping with one another, making the variables unreadable. Google gave me the code: theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = #, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)). I first tried with angle = 45, then tries angle = 90 and I liked that better.
```

6. Create a graph of character's height by mass. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height)) + geom_violin()
```

7.Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(mass, height)) + geom_boxplot(color="black", fill="seagreen4") + theme_classic() + xlab("Mass (kg)") + ylab("Height (cm)") + ggtitle("Character Height by Mass")
``` 

8. Add gender as a third variable to your graph of height by mass. 
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(x=mass, y=height, fill=gender)) + geom_boxplot()
```

9. Customize your graph to make it more presentable. Consider color, backgrounds, axes, etc.
```{r}
ggplot(starwars, aes(x=mass, y=height, fill=gender)) + geom_boxplot() + theme_classic() + scale_fill_manual(values=c("masculine"="cadetblue", "feminine"="pink")) + xlab("Mass (kg)") + ylab("Height (cm)") + ggtitle("Character Height and Mass by Gender") + theme(legend.position="top")
```
